headline: Medium risk: MemMachine’s MCP/API outputs can be misused as trusted input, while RisingWave’s data-engineering role creates downstream conflict and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so its outputs can be bridged into another agent’s input. RisingWave has no documented parser hardening or provenance checks, so if it consumes MemMachine content through a shared workspace or MCP path, prompt injection is plausible. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is copied into RisingWave prompts or jobs via MCP/shared files
IF RisingWave treats external text as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MemMachine-generated text into RisingWave workflows
Add a provenance tag to all MemMachine outputs before handoff
Require a human review step before any RisingWave action on agent-generated content
Restrict MCP access to read-only, non-executable payloads
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and has allowlisted network egress, but RisingWave shows no data classes touched and no egress. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is possible only if an operator explicitly routes sensitive MemMachine context into RisingWave. The blast radius appears limited by the profiles.
conditions: IF the operator forwards MemMachine context containing sensitive user facts into RisingWave inputs
IF RisingWave is deployed with a shared workspace or logs that retain those inputs
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive MemMachine context into RisingWave jobs
Separate logs and workspaces for the two agents
Redact user facts before handoff
Review network destinations allowed for MemMachine
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine can use MCP and network egress, while RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no documented write surfaces or concurrency model here. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so direct write-write conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because RisingWave’s write paths are undocumented in the profile, so I choose the lower documented risk rather than inventing capabilities.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external resource through an undocumented bridge
IF an operator maps MemMachine MCP actions onto RisingWave mutable state
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate resources
Disable write actions in MemMachine MCP where possible
Use a single orchestrator to serialize any shared updates
Audit for shared database or filesystem targets
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit conversational outputs through API/MCP, and RisingWave could plausibly consume those outputs in a data pipeline. If RisingWave treats MemMachine text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream transformations or materialized views. The profiles do not document verification gates, so the interaction is inferred and I escalate above low because the downstream blast radius can affect multiple work products.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests MemMachine-generated text or facts as pipeline input
IF no validation step checks those facts before transformation or publication
mitigations: Insert a validation step before RisingWave consumes MemMachine output
Mark MemMachine output as untrusted by default
Limit downstream jobs to non-production datasets
Add schema and range checks on all ingested fields
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while RisingWave’s profile does not declare regulated data handling or residency constraints. No direct residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen flows of sensitive data into a general data-engineering system. I do not cite RisingWave data classes because none are listed.
conditions: IF long-term user facts are exported from MemMachine into RisingWave storage or logs
IF those records are subject to retention or deletion obligations
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into RisingWave unless necessary
Set short retention on any shared logs
Document deletion/export handling for MemMachine-derived records
Review residency of any external storage used
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for retention and deletion
